Fantasy contests remain a small part of the picture. Operators reported $837,938 in adjusted revenues for September 2026 and paid $70,387 in taxes.

Sources indicate that detroit’s land-based results now set a baseline for Michigan’s October online casino and sports betting figures, which come next. In September, the state’s commercial and tribal online operators took in $355.7 million in combined iGaming and online sports betting gross receipts, 5.4% more than in August.

It has been revealed that every e-commerce grid, product page and checkout screen is a shelf. Merchandisers have spent decades working out what to put at eye level, how many choices to show and how to tell whether a display works, and web teams are now rebuilding the same logic in code: sort orders, pinned products, badges, filters and A/B tests. Knowing where those ideas came from helps you build them with fewer mistakes.

According to recent reports, this article maps physical retail merchandising onto digital product design. It covers visual hierarchy and choice load in listing UIs, a small rule-based ranking function you can test, accessible price and badge design with a contrast checker, and a significance test for layout experiments. It also covers why good intends fail at the handoff between design, engineering and operations. The numbers in the examples are illustrative, so use your own data. The code was run with Node.js 22.

Merchandising shapes how products are displayed, promoted and made accessible across sales channels. A well-planned strategy considers visual hierarchy, packaging, promotional materials, inventory timing and consistency between locations. For example, a skincare product may struggle to convert if testers are missing, shelf information is unclear or displays arrive after a campaign begins. If you build for the web, nearly every one of these problems has a direct counterpart:.

Customers scan before they read. Nielsen Norman Group defines visual hierarchy as the arrangement of elements so the eye moves through them in order of importance, and names color and contrast, scale and grouping as the main tools. On a shelf, a larger facing or a contrasting background makes the hero product visible first. In a product grid, the equivalents are a larger card for a featured item, a clear boundary around a bundle, and a restrained use of badges so that only one or two items carry emphasis.

A common mistake is giving every card a badge, a color and a call to action. When everything is emphasized, nothing is, and the page reads like a crowded table in a store. Treat emphasis as a limited resource and have the design system say how many emphasized cards one screen may show.

A premium item placed beside entry-level alternatives may lose perceived value, and a crowded display can make fresh products look less appealing. Hick’s Law states that the time to make a decision increases with the number and complexity of choices, and its practical advice is to reduce options when speed matters and to highlight recommended ones. In a listing UI that suggests a curated first screen with a clear sort label, a few high-confidence recommendations and filters that handle the long tail, rather than an unbroken wall of products. Hick’s Law is a guide, not a rule, so treat it as a hypothesis to test on your own audience.

Merchandisers often ask for things like “pin the new range to the top, boost this collection, never show more than two items from one brand in a row, and push sold-out items down”. Implemented as scattered CSS order values and one-off queries, these requests become hard to audit. A small, pure function keeps the rules explicit and testable.

Because the function has no side effects, a short test can check every rule. This one confirms that pinned items lead, a pinned item that is out of stock is skipped, the brand cap pushes a third item from one brand behind other brands, sold-out items go last and a boost can lift a weaker product:.

The design decision here is that stock demotion and the brand cap are defaults, while pins and boosts are inputs a merchandiser can change without a deploy, for example from a config file or admin screen. A real system would also log which rule moved each item, so that someone can answer why a product appears where it does.

In a recent development, price cards and shelf labels are text, and text needs contrast. The WCAG contrast requirement asks for at least 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text. Product cards are a place where this slips, because grey secondary prices and pastel sale badges look refined in a mockup. The following script computes the WCAG contrast ratio, so you can run it over your design tokens in CI.

Recent findings suggest that it prints 4.54 for mid grey #767676 on white, which just passes for normal text, 7.00 for #595959, which would also meet the stricter enhanced level, and 3.96 for the pink #d94f70, which fails for small badge text but would pass for large text. A sale badge that fails the check should be fixed in the token, not on one page.

A useful display respects the realities of the sales environment: floor space, customer movement, staff workload, replenishment access and how much information shoppers can absorb at a glance. The digital version is the gap between the design file and what ships. Test the setup with the people who will use it, not only with the team that created it, because their feedback reveals practical problems before a wide rollout.

Sources indicate that A polished plan can fail in practice when materials arrive late, displays are assembled incorrectly or teams miss replenishment. On the web, the matching failures are a promotion that goes live before its product data is synced, a badge that stays on after a sale ends, and a hero banner that links to a discontinued item. Execution needs coordination across marketing, suppliers, logistics and engineering, with clear instructions, realistic schedules, display standards and checks. Some companies outsource this kind of field merchandising. One provider’s services page, for example, lists planogram and retail resets, end-cap displays, signage placement, on-shelf availability, in-store audits and visit reporting. Whether or not you hire help, that list is a useful checklist of what execution involves, and most items have a digital twin you can automate: availability checks, expiry dates on promotions and audit reports. Treat any performance figures on vendor pages as the vendor’s own claims and ask for evidence before relying on them.

Timing matters most for seasonal promotions and limited windows. A campaign that goes live after peak demand has passed cannot deliver the same value, so give promotional content a start and end date in the data model and have a scheduled job remove it, rather than relying on someone to remember.

Sources indicate that sales alone cannot tell you whether visibility, placement, stockouts, confusing information or poor setup caused a result. For a web listing, the answer is a controlled experiment. The script below compares conversion for a control grid and a variant with a two-proportion z-test, a standard way to check whether a difference is larger than chance would explain.

Recent findings suggest that with these illustrative numbers, conversion rises from 3.00 percent to 3.90 percent, a relative lift of 30.0 percent, and the z value of 2.21 exceeds the 1.96 threshold for roughly 95 percent confidence. That does not prove the curated grid is better in general. It says this difference is unlikely to be noise for this test, and it assumes you fixed the sample size in advance and did not stop the moment the result looked good. Use a proper experimentation platform or a statistician for anything with real revenue at stake.

A strong merchandising operation does not require a large budget. A simple guide for product priorities, layout, pricing, replenishment and approved materials keeps execution consistent, and it is the physical version of a design system: a small set of approved components and rules that make the correct result the easy path. For a product card, that means a documented component with a fixed set of badge types, a defined maximum of emphasized items per screen and tokens that already pass the contrast check.

It has been revealed that consistency also protects trust. Damaged fixtures, inconsistent packaging, missing prices and outdated signs make good products look poorly managed, and the digital equivalents are broken images, stale prices and mismatched labels between the listing and the product page. Aim for consistency, not identical pages: a mobile grid and a kiosk screen can differ, but they should share product priorities, visual identity and core messages.

Sources indicate that temporary and in-store selling spaces demand quick communication. Visitors move fast, attention is limited, and interfaces must be clear from a distance and forgiving of mistakes. If you build kiosk, tablet or point-of-sale software, these constraints shape the interface:.

According to recent reports, when results disappoint, audit the real experience before commissioning a redesign. Think like a first-time customer: is the offer clear, are premium items distinct and can the team maintain the page easily? Government small-business guidance offers concrete analogues. The Queensland Government’s retail display guidance recommends showing essential information and prices so customers can decide rapidly, placing popular or profitable items at eye level, and refreshing window displays every two to four weeks. The Westminster City Council guide similarly links visual merchandising, layout and planned promotions to attracting customers and encouraging them to spend more time and money in a business.

Prioritize visibility, clarity, stock accuracy and consistent execution before investing in a full redesign. Small operational improvements can make a meaningful difference, especially when they remove obstacles that repeatedly interrupt the buying process.

The public guidance cited here was written for general small-business use, and UX principles such as visual hierarchy and Hick’s Law come from interface research, so they are useful analogies rather than guarantees. The code is a teaching sketch: it ignores personalization, pagination, caching, search relevance and many other concerns of a production ranking system. Results vary with category, audience and device, so test changes in your own setting and treat any benchmark as a starting point.

What is merchandising in e-commerce? It is how products are displayed, ordered, promoted and made accessible across a site or app, including layout, labels, badges, sort rules and inventory handling.

According to recent reports, how does visual hierarchy apply to a product grid? The same tools apply: contrast, scale and grouping decide what the eye sees first and which products read as related.

What should I measure first? Start with conversion, add-to-cart rate and stock availability for the listing, then add average order value and revenue per visitor once the basics are tracked.

Recent findings suggest that how do I know a layout test is reliable? Fix the sample size in advance, randomize consumers, run it long enough to cover weekly patterns and check significance, for example with the two-proportion test above.

Do small teams need a major design system? No. A short component guide with a few badge types, spacing rules and accessible color tokens is enough to keep pages consistent.

Industry observers note that merchandising is applied interface design with a long history. Clear hierarchy, a curated first screen, readable prices, explicit ranking rules and controlled experiments carry over directly from the shelf to the screen. For designers and developers, the practical lesson is that a good layout only counts if it ships correctly, stays current and is measured. Audit the basics, put the rules in code, test one change at a time and record what you learn.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • West Virginia's online casinos posted record monthly revenue in October 2026, the second full month with bet365 live in the state.
  • The revenue measure is adjusted gross interactive wagering receipts.
  • According to recent reports, bet365 launched online sports betting and casino in the state on Aug.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Virginia's online casinos posted record monthly revenue in October 2026, the second full month with bet365 live in the state. The result pushed 2026 revenue past the total for all of 2025, while a bill to raise the iGaming tax remains pending.

The revenue measure is adjusted gross interactive wagering receipts. State law defines it as an operator’s gross online wagering receipts minus winnings paid to players. Under 2019’s House Bill 2934, the privilege tax on those receipts goes into the Interactive Wagering Fund each week, and every licensed racetrack and historic resort pays it.

According to recent reports, bet365 launched online sports betting and casino in the state on Aug. 27, 2026. West Virginia is its fourth U.S. online casino state. In its other 14 states, bet365 offers sports betting only.

Lottery licensing documents show bet365 received an interim license in January 2026. It was approved for a full annual license on July 29. West Virginia was the tech giant’s sixth North American launch in 13 months, Yogonet reported. The earlier introduces were Kansas and Maryland in August 2025, Missouri in December 2025, Michigan in April 2026 and Alberta in July 2026.

Industry observers note that west Virginia’s market has a fixed structure. The Interactive Wagering Act allows no more than five gaming facility licenses with online wagering. Every online game counts as a state-owned lottery game. October’s record is consistent with bet365 adding to that market, but the operator split has yet to be shown.

Recent findings suggest that two months of 2026 remain to be reported. The comparison months set a high bar. Adjusted gross interactive gaming receipts were $37,198,210 in November 2025. Receipts for the fiscal year to date through Nov. 30, 2025, were $169,425,990.

Industry observers note that the broader lottery picture also demonstrates growth. The Lottery took in more than $1.33 billion in gross revenue in fiscal 2026, which ended June 30. It sent $582.9 million to the state. Revenue was $58 million higher than in fiscal 2025. In its fiscal 2026 wrap-up, the Lottery named iLottery and iGaming as its biggest growth areas, and stated iGaming was following national gaming trends.

In a recent development, higher revenue also raises the stakes of a pending tax change. Introduced on Jan. 16, 2026, House Bill 4397 would increase the iGaming privilege tax. The bill is still listed as pending in the House Local Governments Committee.

The next detail to watch is the operator breakdown. The Lottery publishes a file that splits interactive wagering data by skin and casino. That file will show how much of October’s record came from bet365.

Michigan clears Soaring Eagle to swap GAN for White Hat Gaming’s platform

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (618 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Readwrite

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Michigan's regulator has approved the Saginaw Chippewa Indian Tribe's move of its Soaring Eagle online casino and sportsbook from GAN to White Hat Gaming.
  • Soaring Eagle Gaming has a newly introduced technology partner in Michigan.
  • Platform swaps like this are rare in Michigan.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Michigan's regulator has approved the Saginaw Chippewa Indian Tribe's move of its Soaring Eagle online casino and sportsbook from GAN to White Hat Gaming. The rare platform swap gives White Hat a full platform role in a top-three US market while GAN's owner restructures the business.

Soaring Eagle Gaming has a newly introduced technology partner in Michigan. The Saginaw Chippewa Indian Tribe’s online casino and online sports betting operations now run on White Hat Gaming Inc.’s platform. White Hat replaces GAN, which had powered the tribe’s Michigan offer since launch. That launch came under the Eagle Casino and Sports brand.

Platform swaps like this are rare in Michigan. Players keep the same Soaring Eagle brand.

The board reviewed the White Hat platform and the tribe’s branding submission before signing off. The tribe also filed a signed agreement with White Hat. Every supplier and vendor needed for launch had already been approved. Executive Director Henry Williams stated the board checked the new platform carefully against its standards on integrity, security and consumer protection, which apply to any platform Michigan players use.

According to recent reports, the approval carries conditions. Both companies are limited to games, sports events and bet types the board has approved, and must route business through approved suppliers, vendors and payment locations. Both companies must also fully adopt all internal control amendments the board has approved.

In a recent development, the board’s list of authorized platform providers now names White Hat as the tribe’s provider for online casino and online sports betting. The tribe already had a content tie to White Hat Studios, the games supplier. In June 2022, White Hat Studios announced it would supply branded games, including Ted, Deal or No Deal and Peaky Blinders, to the tribe’s PlayEagle.com site.

Industry observers note that the stakes in Michigan remain sizable. Operators reported $355.7 million in combined online casino and online sports betting gross receipts for September 2026, up 5.4% from August. Online casino accounted for $300.2 million and sports betting for $55.5 million. Adjusted gross receipts came to $313.04 million. Online casino adjusted receipts, however, fell 0.9% from August. The figures are consistent with a market still growing year on year but flatter month to month.

The switch comes as GAN works through changes under fresh ownership. In results for the six months to September 30, 2026, Sega Sammy mentioned GAN is running a turnaround program that cuts fixed costs. The program will also move GAN ahead with migrating to a new platform. Adding GAN and Stakelogic raised group sales. It also widened the operating loss compared with the same period a year earlier.

It has been revealed that november 9-13 is Illegal Gambling Awareness Week. We're proud to partner with International Association of Gaming Regulators (IAGR) to raise awareness about the risks of illegal gambling. Regulation helps protect players. Illegal operators intentionally operate outside the law,… pic.twitter.com/WhKHVIdVZJ.

— Michigan Gaming Control Board (@MichiganGCB) November 9, 2026.

Industry observers note that white Hat’s own structure is shifting too. Merkur Group agreed in July 2026 to buy the content supplier White Hat Studios for an undisclosed sum. The White Hat Gaming platform and white-label businesses are not part of that deal. They stay with their current owners. The Merkur purchase of White Hat Studios remains pending regulatory approval.
